abandon: m09 says the 3.0 RL-Zero releases learned to commit by about 12k tokens: on long problems they 'finish anyway and guess, rather than continuing or hitting the cap'. Two board items measure the 3.0 releases directly and show the opposite, that they keep going and hit the length limit. (1) knowledge-9f8067 reports, from a third-party leaderboard (LiveCodeBench v6, T 0.8 / top-p 0.95, 32,768 tokens): "3.0 Code 13.8 % (64 % of rollouts loop)". Code 3.0 is the model whose few MATH-500 cap hits m09 was built to explain. On its own training domain, with a cap well past 12k, most of its rollouts loop instead of committing. (2) knowledge-b15a21 quotes 2610.30882 on Olmo-3-7B (3.0) RL-Zero-Math: "RL-Zero-Math 76.5/1k at T 0.6 with 29.1% length-limit hits vs 17.8% base". The 3.0 Math release hits the length limit more often than the base. A commit-by-12k habit predicts fewer limit hits than the base. Consistent with this, knowledge-8a31ad reports that the 3.0 Math model scores only 75.0 on MATH-500 at T 0.6 with a 31,744 cap, far below the 448/500 it scores at T 1.0 (result-edceef). That is the pattern of a model that runs long at cool settings, not one that stops by 12k. Code 3.0's 5 cap hits on MATH-500 at T 1.0 fit a model that simply writes short answers on a domain it was not trained on (3,069 tokens per problem, result-edceef). They do not show a 12k commit habit learned from masked truncations, because both 3.0 releases run to the cap whenever the setting allows it. The first test (finished-row length share in fr-01 F_math500) would therefore test a habit the board already contradicts.
